subject: SIG evidence: MetroHealth retention inventory & deletion proof
messages:
From: Carmen Ruiz <carmen.ruiz@metrohealth.org>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@metrohealth.org>
Date: 2026-04-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG questionnaire — retention & deletion evidence

Jordan,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG review and internal audit we need a couple of concrete artifacts related to Redwood's data retention and deletion practices for our tenant(s). Specifically MetroHealth needs: 

- A retention inventory (per-data-type TTLs, retention justification)
- Evidence that deletions are executed (sample deletion event logs, IDs, timestamps)
- Any lifecycle policy IDs (S3/GCS) or config snapshots showing automatic expiry rules
- Clarification on customer-requested exceptions (we may need a 365d TTL for clinical_treatment_logs vs. your default 90d)

Can you provide these items or confirm what you can provide by COB 2026-05-05? If you need specific tenant or dataset identifiers, let me know and I can supply them. We prefer redacted samples rather than full PHI.

Attached our SIG export with the retention section highlighted.

Thanks,
Carmen Ruiz
Security & Compliance Manager
MetroHealth Systems

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Carmen Ruiz <carmen.ruiz@metrohealth.org>
Date: 2026-04-27T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — retention & deletion evidence

Hi Carmen — thanks for the clear ask. We're able to produce the items you requested; here's the plan: 

1) Retention inventory spreadsheet (per-data-type TTLs, retention reason): I'll send a populated sheet and a template so your team can cross-check.
2) Deletion evidence: sample deletion event logs with event IDs & timestamps (redacted IDs where necessary), and a brief explanation of how deletion is cascaded through caches/KV stores.
3) Lifecycle rules: copies/screenshots of S3 lifecycle policies and the internal rule IDs.
4) Exception path: outline of how we approve short-term customer exceptions and suggested attestation wording.

I attached a retention-inventory-template.csv — please confirm which tenant(s) you want us to inventory (tenant name/tenant id). We can deliver initial artifacts by 2026-05-03 and final packet by 2026-05-05 if you need formal sign-off.

Two quick questions: 1) Is anonymized/redacted samples acceptable for deletion logs? 2) Can you confirm the exact resource name for "clinical_treatment_logs" so we can validate if it maps to a single object type or multiple streams?

Will loop in our security/compliance folks to assemble the packet.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: retention-inventory-template.csv (spreadsheet template)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-27T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: FW: SIG questionnaire — retention & deletion evidence

Team — forwarding MetroHealth's request (see attached PDF). They want retention inventory + deletion evidence and are asking for a potential exception (90d -> 365d) for "clinical_treatment_logs."

Can you help with the following by EOD 2026-05-01: 
- Marissa: Gather sample deletion events (IDs + timestamps), lifecycle policy screenshots, and the typical retention matrix we provide for SOC2/SIG customers. If we need legal approval for an exception, flag it here.
- Neha: Draft a short attestation paragraph we can provide to MetroHealth that describes the scope of artifacts and the redaction standard for samples.
- Olga: Confirm whether retention for the relevant resource is enforced via S3 lifecycle rules or internal TTLs and list the policy IDs.

I attached the retention-inventory-template.csv — please populate rows you can and return. I will coordinate with Jordan to deliver to MetroHealth on 2026-05-03 (initial) and follow up by 2026-05-05 with final packet.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-28T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: SIG questionnaire — retention & deletion evidence

Jordan/Team — thanks, I'll take point on evidence collection. Quick notes on deliverables and what I'll attach: 

- Retention matrix (per-data-type TTLs) — see retention-matrix-metrohealth.xlsx (attached).
- Lifecycle rules: screenshots + rule IDs for the buckets that store MetroHealth artifacts (rl-7412, rl-7420).
- Deletion evidence: we'll provide three redacted deletion events per resource (event IDs, timestamps, initiating service). We'll show how KV cache invalidation is triggered and include an example of the propagation timeline.
- Logs: audit log extracts showing admin-initiated deletion operations (redacted).

About the requested exception for "clinical_treatment_logs": we generally default to 90d for non-PHI telemetry. Clinical logs are borderline PHI-sensitive and extending to 365d requires a documented business need and legal sign-off. We can provide an interim attestation that we will retain for 365d for that resource pending legal approval, but we should include: scope, duration of the exception, and controls for access/audit.

Neha — can you draft the attestation language that limits the exception to a specific tenant id and includes audit obligations?

I will populate the retention-matrix and export the sample deletion events by 2026-05-01.

Marissa Cole
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: retention-matrix-metrohealth.xlsx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Carmen Ruiz <carmen.ruiz@metrohealth.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-02T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — retention & deletion evidence

Carmen — quick update and delivery plan. Per Marissa's work we'll provide the following by 2026-05-03 (initial packet):

- Retention inventory spreadsheet (populated): per-data-type TTLs + rationale (attachment and Drive link).
- Lifecycle policy screenshots and rule IDs (rl-7412, rl-7420).
- Three redacted deletion event samples per resource (event ID, timestamp, initiating service).
- Audit log extract showing deletion initiation and propagation.
- Suggested attestation language and an exception process (if MetroHealth confirms the tenant id and business justification we can scope a temporary 365d exception for clinical_treatment_logs pending legal sign-off).

Deliverables will be available via the Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/metrohealth/retention-evidence and I'll attach the retention matrix as a first pass (retention-matrix-metrohealth.xlsx). For DocuSign attestation, please confirm the signatory and we'll generate an envelope (DocuSign: 0-XYZ-12345).

Two asks from your side to expedite: 
1) Provide the tenant id(s) we should inventory (or confirm that we should use tenant: metrohealth-prod).
2) Confirm if redacted samples are acceptable; we will not provide any PHI in the artifacts.

If acceptable I will schedule a quick 20m sync with Marissa/Neha to walk through the evidence packet.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: retention-matrix-metrohealth.xlsx
